definitions.Pi: Pi(y,y') subseteq {3,4}^2, represented by four feasibility bits q33,q34,q43,q44.
definitions.equivalence: pair x equiv_Pi pair x' iff Pi(x)=Pi(x').

Q1_16_CLASS_BOUND.proof: Pi is a subset of a four-element set {3,4}^2, so there are exactly at most 2^4=16 possible Pi masks.

Q2_EXACTNESS.proof: Within one Pi-equality class, every pair has exactly the same frozen semantic target Pi by definition.

proof: Let E be any equivalence relation whose class summary preserves Pi exactly.
If two pairs have different Pi values, placing them in the same E-class would force one class summary to represent two different target values and would violate exact preservation.
Therefore every E-class is contained in a Pi-equality class.
Hence every exact quotient relative solely to target Pi refines Pi-equality; Pi-equality is the coarsest/maximal exact semantic quotient for that target.

Q4_COMPUTABILITY_SEPARATION.proof: The existence and cardinality of the Pi quotient are semantic facts only. Computing the four feasibility bits is exactly the unresolved discovery problem; no extension-oracle-free algorithm follows from Q1-Q3.

consequence.remaining_problem: Polynomial graph-discoverable computation of q33,q34,q43,q44 without invoking the original extension oracle.
